I picked up The Hunter:Call of the Wild on sale recently. While you don't have direct competition it's a really solid hunting game and innawoods simulator and you can play with small groups of friends. Shooting mechanics feel satisfying and has some progression to it, with perks depending on which weapons you use most. Larger animals can charge and even kill you if you're not careful.

Gorgeous scenery to boot. Warning that it's not an extremely fast paced game - you might spend 15-30 minutes between seeing animals to shoot while you're out exploring.

I have a friend that plays it occasionally, considered the idea of picking it up. can you mix and match hunting options, like one with a rifle and another with a bow? and is there any perks to working together instead of just competing for the biggest kill?

A buddy and I often play together but we are usually just roaming around different parts of the map - there are three maps (including DLC) and all of them are enormous in size. In terms of co-op it's always helpful to have an extra pair of eyes to spot your targets, and spotting a deert will highlight it for the other player as well. If two people hit the same deer it gives credit to both based on how good each individual shot was (this is true in general-clean kills like heart and lung shots are worth much more than a gut shot). Two people make more noise than one, though, and deert might hear you coming.

As far as weapons go the regular hunting rifles seem to be the best all around, but the other weapons are still highly effective and have perks of their own. I haven't used much besides the rifles so I can't speak much about specifics. It takes a bit of unlocking but you can tailor your character how you like - from a long distance sharpshooter to a sneaky ambush bow hunter and anything in between.

I will again stress that this game is not very fast paced. Most of it is walking innawoods and looking for deert doodies. Much more casual and relaxing than most multiplayer shooters.
